sky-temple.lede: A floating Japanese island in cube art — a five-tier pagoda, torii gate, waterfall, drifting petals and a 60-second day/night cycle.
sky-temple.prompt:
Build one complete, self-contained web demo: a floating Japanese island in the sky, voxel/cube art style, cinematic and alive. It must look like a crafted scene, not a tech demo.

DELIVERABLE
A single HTML file, self-contained: all HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline. Three.js r160 via importmap from unpkg — "three": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js and "three/addons/": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/ — ES modules, OrbitControls from three/addons. Nothing else external: no images, textures, models, fonts or audio files — every surface, shape and effect must be generated procedurally in code (canvas-generated textures are fine). No build step, no TypeScript, no npm, no frameworks. Opening the file in a browser must work with zero console errors.

SCENE — all of the following must be present
1. The island: an irregular floating landmass built from cubes — grass top layer, dirt and rock strata beneath, tapered underside so it reads as torn from the earth. The edge must be uneven, never a circle.
2. A five-tier pagoda (cube-built): alternating wall bands, wide dark roofs with upturned corners (scaled boxes are fine), gold finial. It is the visual anchor — put it on the high point.
3. A torii gate at the head of a stone path that climbs to the pagoda, stone lanterns along it with warm emissive glow, and a small cluster of cube houses with lantern-lit windows. A small reflecting pond with stone edging sits near the base.
4. Vegetation: cube-style pines in clusters plus one large cherry tree with a pink cube canopy near the pagoda.
5. A waterfall pouring off one edge of the island, with mist particles where it disappears into the clouds below.
6. A sea of clouds below the island: several layered semi-transparent cloud slabs plus drifting cloud puffs, giving real depth far below.
7. Cherry-blossom petals drifting across the scene (200+ instanced), and two or three small flocks of birds circling.
8. Sky: vertical gradient, sun and moon, stars that appear at night, soft distance fog tinted to the time of day.

ANIMATION & LIGHTING
- The island slowly bobs and tilts, as if drifting in air (subtle — a few degrees max).
- Full day/night cycle on a ~60 second loop: dawn, noon, golden sunset, night. Sun/moon orbit the scene, light colour and fog follow, lanterns and windows glow at night, stars fade in.
- Continuous motion everywhere: waterfall, mist, petals, clouds, pond shimmer, birds.
- Soft shadows; warm rim light at sunset.

CAMERA & CONTROLS
- Damped OrbitControls with sensible limits (cannot go under the island or inside the pagoda).
- A "Cinematic" toggle button: slowly orbits the island at a low dramatic angle with gentle drift; toggles back to free orbit.
- A "Pause time" toggle for the day/night cycle.

PERFORMANCE
- Stable 60fps at 1080p on a mid-range laptop: use InstancedMesh for cubes, petals and clouds; keep draw calls low; cap pixel ratio at 2; handle resize.
- All procedural placement uses a seeded PRNG (mulberry32, seed 1337) so the island is IDENTICAL on every load.

UI
Minimal corner overlay: title "SKY TEMPLE", one-line hint ("Drag to orbit · Scroll to zoom"), the two toggle buttons. Fade to low opacity after 10 seconds idle; restore on mouse move. No other UI. The scene must be screenshot-ready the moment it loads — no interaction needed for the hero shot.

OUTPUT
Return the complete file as one HTML code block. No explanations, no commentary before or after.

living-city.lede: A city that builds itself at load — rush-hour traffic, working traffic lights, a river with bridges and a 90-second day/night cycle.
living-city.prompt:
Build one complete, self-contained web demo: a living procedural city — generated fresh in code, full of traffic, lit through a day/night cycle. It must feel like a real place you could fly through, not a grid of grey boxes.

DELIVERABLE
A single HTML file, self-contained: all HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline. Three.js r160 via importmap from unpkg — "three": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js and "three/addons/": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/ — ES modules. Nothing else external: no images, textures, models or fonts — everything generated in code (canvas-generated textures are fine). No build step, no TypeScript, no npm, no frameworks. Zero console errors when opened.

THE CITY (all of the following)
1. Procedural layout, one generator run at load: a central downtown of tall towers (up to ~40 floors), a mid-rise ring, low-rise outskirts; a park block with trees and a pond; at least two diagonal avenues cutting across the grid; a river along one edge with two or more bridges. Seeded (mulberry32, seed 1337) — the SAME city every load.
2. Roads: asphalt with lane markings and sidewalks, streetlights along the avenues, traffic lights at major intersections that actually change state.
3. Buildings: window bands, rooftop details (AC units, antennae, water towers), varied palettes, an occasional construction crane; billboards with animated procedural content (draw them with canvas-generated textures).
4. Traffic: cars driving in lanes and stopping at red lights; at night, headlights and tail lights; buses with lit windows; a helicopter circling downtown with a blinking light. Vehicles recycled/instanced — a few hundred max.
5. Day/night cycle (~90 seconds): sky gradient with sun and moon, buildings' windows light up progressively at dusk (vary both per building and per floor), streetlights and billboards come on, light fog, stars at night.

CAMERA
- Damped OrbitControls for free look, plus a "Fly-through" mode button: the camera follows a smooth closed Catmull-Rom spline at street/rooftop level through the city with subtle banking, then toggles back. Minimise clipping through buildings — raise the path above obstacles or nudge points; brief grazes only.

HUD
Small dark translucent overlay: FPS, building count, vehicle count, a day/night pause button, a camera mode button. Small type, tidy.

PERFORMANCE
- Stable 60fps at 1080p on a mid-range laptop: InstancedMesh for buildings, windows, cars and streetlights; distance fog to shorten draw distance; pixel ratio capped at 2; resize handled.

OUTPUT
Return the complete file as one HTML code block. No explanations, no commentary.

neon-drift.lede: A playable synthwave racer — an endless curving highway, boost meter, near-miss bonuses and a fully synthesised soundtrack.
neon-drift.prompt:
Build one complete, self-contained web demo: a playable synthwave racer — NEON DRIFT. You chase-cam a hovercraft down an endless, procedurally curving neon highway at dusk. It must be fun within five seconds, with real game feel.

DELIVERABLE
A single HTML file, self-contained: all HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline. Three.js r160 via importmap from unpkg — "three": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js and "three/addons/": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/ — ES modules. No assets: every visual generated in code (canvas-generated textures fine), all sound synthesized with WebAudio — no audio files. No build step, no TypeScript, no npm. Zero console errors.

TRACK & WORLD
1. Endless procedural track: segments that curve left/right and rise/fall, generated ahead of the player and recycled — it never ends. Seeded (mulberry32, seed 1337) so the course is the same every run.
2. Road: dark asphalt with glowing edge lines and centre dashes; neon pylons or arches passing overhead at intervals; side barriers.
3. Environment: giant striped sun on the horizon, grid ground plane, silhouetted mountain ranges, starfield, occasional neon palm. Violet/magenta fog.

GAMEPLAY
- Controls: left/right arrows or A/D to steer (speed-sensitive steering), Space or Shift to boost with a heat/cooldown meter, R to restart after a crash. Auto-accelerate; top speed increases the longer you survive.
- Hazards: slow rival cars (glowing blocks with tail lights) to dodge; hitting one wrecks you. Near-misses (passing within a small margin) give bonus points with a brief slow-mo flash.
- Scoring: distance plus near-miss bonuses; small "+50 NEAR MISS" popups. Crash: hovercraft bursts into particles, slight camera pull-back, "WRECKED — press R" overlay, best score kept for the session.

GAME FEEL (this is a game-feel test — get it right)
- Camera lags smoothly behind the craft; FOV widens during boost; subtle screen shake on crash and near-miss.
- The craft banks into turns, hovers with a gentle bob; thruster exhaust particles scale with speed.
- Boost adds speed lines in the starfield and a colour shift. Track curvature must telegraph — you can read the next curve before entering it.

AUDIO (WebAudio, synthesized, no files)
- Engine hum whose pitch follows speed; whoosh on near-miss; explosion noise on crash; a simple looping synthwave bass/arp underneath. Audio starts on first click (autoplay policy); M mutes.

HUD
Speed, score, best, boost meter. Title card "NEON DRIFT" with a "Press any key to drive" prompt; instructions live on the title card only.

PERFORMANCE
- 60fps at 1080p: instancing for pylons and particles, recycled objects (no unbounded arrays), pixel ratio capped at 2, resize handled.

OUTPUT
Return the complete file as one HTML code block. No explanations, no commentary.

pulse-engine.lede: A generative instrument — a drum machine and synth that compose on their own while a particle galaxy pulses on the beat.
pulse-engine.prompt:
Build one complete, self-contained web demo: PULSE ENGINE — a generative audiovisual instrument. It plays music by itself, you can steer it, and the visuals are driven by the sound. This is an audio-engineering and aesthetics test.

DELIVERABLE
A single HTML file, self-contained: all HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline. Three.js r160 via importmap from unpkg ("three": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js, "three/addons/": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/) allowed for the visuals. No assets of any kind — all sound must be synthesized in WebAudio (no samples, no audio files); all imagery generated in code. No build step, no TypeScript, no npm. Zero console errors.

AUDIO ENGINE
1. A 16-step sequencer with four synthesized drum voices — kick, snare, hats, clap — each built from oscillators/noise with real envelopes. Pattern editable by clicking steps in the UI.
2. A bassline and an arpeggio synth (subtractive: oscillator + filter + envelope) playing a seeded four-chord progression, key and mood of your choice (stay in key — it must sound musical).
3. Generative mode, ON by default: a seeded composer (seed 1337) mutates patterns and melodies over time so it never exactly repeats, while staying musical — the kind of loop you'd leave running, not random beeps. A "Randomise" button reseeds it.
4. Rock-solid timing: no audible jitter or drift — all note events scheduled against AudioContext.currentTime (lookahead scheduling, not per-step setTimeout).
5. A master chain with soft limiting so it never clips, whatever the user clicks; master volume and mute.
6. Transport: Play/Stop and a tempo slider 90–160 BPM.

VISUALS (Three.js)
- A full-viewport scene reacting live through an AnalyserNode: for example a slowly rotating particle galaxy that pulses on the kick, warps with the bass, sparkles on hats, with a radial spectrum ring for mids/highs and slow camera drift. It must look composed, not like a debug spectrum.
- Cohesive synthwave palette (deep blue/purple/cyan/magenta), additive blending, glow via sprites or additive planes (no post-processing dependency needed).

UI
- A start overlay: "CLICK TO START AUDIO" (browsers block autoplay) — everything begins on the first click.
- A slim bottom bar: Play/Stop, tempo, mute, Generative on/off, Randomise. Small keyboard hotkeys: 1–4 mute individual drums, G toggles generative; list the hotkeys in one small help line.

QUALITY BAR
- Audio first: clean, mixed and musical (kick audible, bass warm, hats crisp); no clicks or pops when patterns change (envelopes must handle note starts/stops).
- The visuals must visibly lock to the beat — the kick pulse unmistakable.
- 60fps at 1080p with audio running; pixel ratio capped at 2.

OUTPUT
Return the complete file as one HTML code block. No explanations, no commentary.

cloth-lab.lede: A from-scratch cloth physics lab — drag it, tear it, switch on the wind, drop balls on it. The solver is hand-written; no physics library.
cloth-lab.prompt:
Build one complete, self-contained web demo: a cloth and rigid-body physics lab, with the physics written from scratch. This is a simulation-quality test.

DELIVERABLE
A single HTML file, self-contained: all HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline. Three.js r160 via importmap from unpkg — "three": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js and "three/addons/": https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/ — ES modules, OrbitControls from three/addons. No assets. No build step, no TypeScript, no npm. Zero console errors.
NO physics libraries: cannon-es, ammo, rapier, physx, matter.js and the like are banned. Write the solver yourself (Verlet/XPBD or similar) — not a reworded copy of a published tutorial implementation.

THE SIMULATION
1. A cloth sheet — a grid of at least 60 x 40 = 2400 particles — pinned at its two top corners, hanging like a curtain between two posts. Structural, shear and bend constraints. It must drape and fold naturally with zero jitter at rest.
2. A solid sphere pedestal near the cloth that the cloth drapes over when pulled across it (cloth-vs-sphere collision).
3. A floor at ground level (cloth-vs-floor collision); gravity 9.8.
4. Interaction:
   - Left-drag any cloth particle: grab it (spring to cursor) and fling the cloth — it must ripple believably.
   - T key or right-click on the cloth: tear it — remove that particle's constraints so it splits and hangs open; for a few seconds after a tear, springs under high strain should keep breaking.
   - W: toggle gusty wind (smooth time-varying noise, not a constant push).
   - B: spawn 10 falling spheres (radius ~0.2m) that collide with the cloth — the cloth must catch them, drape around them and not explode.
   - R: reset the scene.
5. Fixed-timestep simulation with an accumulator (never step physics from raw frame delta), with enough solver iterations for stability. It must stay stable for minutes of abuse — flinging, tearing, dozens of balls.

RENDERING
- Cloth as a lit double-sided mesh with subtle sheen (back face must look right when it flips), glossy spheres, soft studio lighting and gentle shadows (real shadow maps or fake blob shadows — either, but the cloth must not look flat). F key toggles a wireframe view of the particle grid.

HUD
Small overlay: title "CLOTH LAB", key hints (drag / T tear / W wind / B balls / F wire / R reset), particle count, sim steps per second.

PERFORMANCE
- 2400+ particles at a comfortable 60fps: typed arrays, no per-frame allocations, flat constraint loops.

QUALITY BAR
- The cloth must look like fabric: no oscillating spikes, no visible interpenetration through itself, graceful tearing (never a whole-sheet explosion).

OUTPUT
Return the complete file as one HTML code block. No explanations, no commentary.
